classification_flags.reason: Client #1 is invoiced manually (the genome itself says so), and the founder can resolve FD-* decisions in code. A resolution UI and status fields are not needed for one client to go review → approve → launch. Suggest GROUND_ZERO_FOUNDATION or POST_FIRST_CLIENT_HIGH_PRIORITY.
One client with founder hand-holding can launch without Sentry. Valuable but not gating; 1d, so cheap to keep in MVP.

With the single-owner model (clientOwnsProject on client_email/client_user_id), only the owner can reach the review endpoints, so role spoofing only lets the owner act as owner. It becomes a real blocker once membership/invites (also a blocker) add collaborators or viewers. It should be bundled with PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_INVITES and not counted separately.
The cited exposure is fixture data (see wrong[]). The remaining real issue, health/model metadata on unauthenticated endpoints, is minor. Hiding the founder page from client accounts is a ~0.5d fix.
Its blocking condition (CI red, so deploy skipped) is the same as CAP.RELEASE.CI_HEALTH. Per AGENTS.md, the frontend ships by manual cPanel ZIP anyway. Fixing CI_HEALTH clears it.

Showing seeded fake projects and sites to a real client is a trust and accuracy problem but does not stop review → approve → launch. Hiding or gating the views would also unblock. Keeping them as blockers is defensible.
MISSING and priority POST_FIRST_CLIENT_HIGH_PRIORITY, yet it is in an MVP work package. A paying client normally needs to download approved deliverables.

Client-private assets go into one public bucket ('live-preview'). It is in an MVP WP but priority is POST_FIRST_CLIENT_HIGH_PRIORITY. For a real client's unreleased brand work, this arguably belongs with the RLS blocker.

marketing provisionMarketingEngagement has no ownership check (only that payment is CONFIRMED), so any authenticated user who knows a paid engagement id can trigger provisioning. Worth stating explicitly.

consistency_issues: Two records are MISSING but carry promotion dispositions: CAP.RISK.RISK_REGISTER (MERGE) and CAP.RUNTIME.PROJECT_ENV_SECRETS (EXPAND). Because of this the genome's promotion dispositions total 205 (CONNECT 38 + EXPAND 48 + RECLASSIFY 13 + REPAIR 45 + MERGE 60 + REBUILD 1), while SITE00_EXISTING_SYSTEM_PROMOTION_PLAN.json lists 203 (EXPAND 47, MERGE 59). The MD's '203 promotions / 44 truly missing' is internally consistent only if those two are treated as ADD; they should be re-dispositioned ADD (or re-statused).

MVP effort 87.0 engineer-days (WP sum) vs 61.0 engineer-days summed from the 30 CLIENT_READY_BLOCKER records' effort_days_estimate. The gap comes from WPs including 5 non-blocker caps and re-estimating per package. The MD does not explain this.
